q: How do I calculate the carbon footprint of rotary or screen printed fabric per metre?
title: Printed fabric carbon footprint per metre
short: Add the print house's fuel for steamers, stenters and dryers and its electricity, convert each and divide by metres printed. Add the greige fabric, pigments, binders and thickeners for the full figure. Curing and steaming are usually the largest energy use.
audience: Fabric printing houses, including Jetpur, Balotra and Surat units

ul: Rotary or flatbed printing machines, and the drying chamber after printing.
Steamer or curing machine to fix the print.
Washing range and stenter for the finish.
Greige or prepared fabric per metre, from your supplier.
Pigment or reactive dyes, binders, thickeners and urea by kg.

p: Report per metre at a stated width and GSM, and say whether the figure covers printing only or greige to finished.

example.title: Worked example: print house per metre (one month)
lines: Plant total: 76,500 / 500,000 = 0.153 kg CO2 per metre
Add the fabric, dyes and binders for the full figure
example.note: Inputs are illustrative; use your own bills and production records.

senseible: Senseible reads the plant's electricity bills (CEA grid factor 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh, CO2 Baseline Database version 21.0) and fuel invoices (IPCC 2006 defaults) into a fingerprinted Scope 1 and 2 record, the plant-level input to a per-unit figure. Bought-in materials go to the supplier evidence trail; product reports are self-declared drafts.
